title: fix(discord): enable voice on supported older hosts
body:
Related: #159773, #159548

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Discord voice failing to load when a newer plugin runs on the supported OpenClaw 2026.9.6 host, whose SDK lacks two newer voice dependencies.

## User Impact

Voice can use the host's supported context loader and worker constructor. On 2026.9.6, context retains the shipped profile-only behavior; the newer multi-session framing remains available on hosts with the shared composer. No configuration, dependency, or host-floor change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Select the modern context composer and CPU-tracked worker factory when supplied by the host. Only an absent capability selects the verified shipped predecessor. Errors from present modern capabilities still propagate. The host continues to own profile loading, and Discord's existing audio transport continues to own worker shutdown.

## Evidence

All evidence below is bound to `418554ad3542cfa54a1e07b41e72ae8ef2cf0b7d` (tree `02ae5f33ab48749389a606022d9645aef28ac679`). [Required CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36340921951), with a 772-second interval from the first job start through the final gate. Full changed-file checks, final typecheck/lint, and independent review passed.

The original source failed four missing-capability regressions. The repaired source passed 83 focused voice tests, including existing cancellation/promotion and worker lifecycle coverage. Final per-file measurements used `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --maxWorkers=1`:

| Test file under `extensions/discord/src/voice/` | Result | Single-worker wall | Vitest duration |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| `ingress.test.ts` | 18 passed | 49.02 s | 38.89 s |
| `audio-worker-thread.test.ts` | 3 passed | 6.06 s | 3.28 s |

The existing ingress file's measured cost is dominated by transformation (83%) and imports (13%); the added cases reuse its owner boundary. The worker cases exercise actual native threads, data transfer, and exit. These are local file timings; the CI run metadata does not expose individual voice-file timings.

Linux/Node 24.19 package proof used the actual npm 2026.9.6 archive, SHA-256 `1a7355691bc0e605222ba818f1f72c1787253c78dfeb0df6be2086ec73b71e63`. Its own CLI lifecycle consumed its pending marker before the immutable-file baseline; all original host members and resolved SDK files subsequently remained unchanged.

- Canonical `pnpm build` passed in 361.465 s. The complete Discord package was built with its original manifest and installed by the old host's CLI. Its emitted lazy voice module loaded, and a voice-enabled empty manager completed its lifecycle.
- A separately identified synthetic package entry exercised the actual candidate voice owners against that host SDK. Cooperative shutdown exited 0 with no termination call. With only the parent's stop command deliberately withheld, the existing transport forced termination exactly once after 2.005 s; native exit was 1 and the adapter retired once.
- Actual legacy context passed default ordered profiles, selected profile, empty-list opt-out, blank files, and a caught host-loader error.
- The canonical Discord entrypoint profiler passed with `qualified: true`, no gaps, matching source/build identity, and verified child/process-group cleanup.

The first proof attempt failed before runtime execution because wrapper resync invalidated linked-worktree Git metadata. Recovery used an independent exact-commit clone and verified all 126,589 retained build/dependency entries plus unchanged build-info/dist hashes before reusing the canonical build. The failure and recovery remain in the evidence. The sealed archive is 108,431,154 bytes, SHA-256 `0d39162ce7472649e3eed81d36fc70dd66a729dfc08aac3738f9f92851ee93b7`; all 1,959 members verified locally.

This proves package linkage, the configured empty manager, and synthetic voice-owner/worker behavior. Live Discord authentication, network provider activation, and audible delivery were not exercised. The owned proof lease was stopped after verification.
